title: "Welcome, student volunteers"
toc: false
---

*An introduction to public health, injury epidemiology and pedestrian safety research, for high school and college students joining our team.*

You may be joining us to label street images, check data, read papers, or help in another way. Whatever the task, it helps to know **why** the work matters and **how** researchers think about it. This orientation covers that.

You don't need any background in public health or statistics. If you're in college and want more detail, look for the **Go deeper** boxes.

## How to use this site

- Go through the modules **in order**. Each takes 20 to 40 minutes.
- Each module ends with a **short quiz**. It isn't graded and nobody sees your score. It's there so you can check yourself.
- Use the **search box** (top right) to find any term. The [Glossary](glossary.qmd) explains the jargon.
- When you finish, go through the [Completion checklist](checklist.qmd) with your supervisor.

## Labeling images?
Do modules **0, 4, 6 and 7** before you start labeling. They explain the rules you'll follow, the data rules, and the reasons for them.
:::

## Questions

Ask your supervisor. There are no silly questions. In research, the person who asks "why do we do it this way?" often catches a mistake.
